title: Society Planning: Model, Simulation And Visualization

context_sources.name: US Bureau of Economic Analysis, personal saving rate
UNESCO Institute for Statistics, education indicators
context_sources.role: Expected and mean years of schooling

limitations: The parameter table has its symbols detached from the names.
The Gini integral and the schooling formula are split across lines.
The income function in the job system is broken across lines and simplified in the code.
The bracket-transition equations repeat symbols, so the balance is read from the prose.
The robustness table has its rows shifted relative to the noise sources.
The MATLAB listing fills the appendix and is not re-run here.

tasks: Define parameters for income, education and equality
Select 10000 founders and compare them with a random draw
Simulate the evolution of jobs, marriages and births
Balance the wage floor against productivity and set parental leave
Test phased immigration on a social network

section_map.summary: Six subproblems, a wage of $33,526 and leave of $50,200.
Six strategies, each answering a stated fear.
Three tiers, word-frequency weights, a checked hierarchy.
Filtered founders against a random control.
Jobs, marriages, births and a sixty-year slump.
Priorities by subgroup and a penalized allocation.
One percent noise over thirty runs.
Judgment parameters, one database, no job competition.

contributions.summary: Weights taken from word frequency, then checked by a consistency ratio.
A selection rule dropped because the control group shows no difference.
A three-objective search narrowed on purpose to half the average income.

dependency_graph.handoff: The income, schooling and output definitions are the attributes the evolution updates
Simulated family incomes and bracket counts feed the three-objective search
The chosen floor and leave pay are the global outcome the allocation tries to protect
The evolution is rerun under each migration plan, and its marriages seed the graph

assumptions.summary: Death depends only on age. No famine, disease or disaster.
No return to Earth. A fresh 10000 arrive if population falls under 1000.
Degree means wealth and connectivity means equality.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: A random sample of 10000 kept as the control.
Pairwise matrices accepted only when the consistency ratio is under 0.1.

models.summary: Income, output and Gini definitions with hierarchy weights.
An agent evolution with marriage by distance.
A three-objective genetic search over five brackets.
A penalized allocation across two groups.
A social graph and a phased migration plan.

verification.summary: Selected founders compared with a random draw on four distributions.
Thirty runs at one percent noise, means and spreads reported.

results_trace.summary: Reported optimum: average income 65234, spread 9848, floor 33526.
Leave pay of 50200 minimizes the spread at 9806.
Phased migration of 50000 beats a single wave in year 50.

writing_logic.summary: Each recommendation answers a fear the reader is assumed to hold.
A criterion is abandoned when the figure shows no effect.
The search is narrowed, and the reason is given before the algorithm.

language_observations.summary: The saving rate is given three readings by its sign.
A hundred years of output is told as a sequence of generations.
A proverb is quoted and then replaced by a distance.
A cost is renamed an investment in the long run.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 2: word cloud, read as equality dominating.
Table 1: parameter list with symbols, tiers and units.
Tables 2 to 4: comparison matrix and the two weight sets.
Figure 3: selection criteria and the four tagged types.
Figures 4 to 11: income, hours, schooling and age, selected against random.
Figure 12: population, output, age and happiness over 100 years.
Figures 13 and 14: a 40-person family network and the marriage ratio.
Figures 15 and 16: output against the wage floor, and the class transitions.
Tables 5 and 6: bracket incomes, shares and the adjusted proportions.
Figure 17: the feasible cloud of the three objectives.
Figures 18 and 19: the leave class and the sweep over leave pay.
Figures 20 and 21: happiness by age and by schooling.
Figures 22 and 23: a 24-person graph and the age pulse.
Figures 24 and 25: five arrival years, and phased against one-year.
Table 8: means and spreads over 30 noisy runs.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Word frequency stands in for a judgment of importance.
The income function is simplified so the program runs on a personal computer.
Degree is assumed to measure wealth with no test.

weaknesses.summary: Several parameters are set by judgment because no source was found.
Job competition is omitted, so long-run unemployment is not credible.
Natural resources and health care are absent, which limits large populations.

independent_extensions.summary: Add competition for jobs so long-run unemployment is real.
Cap population by resources and add health care.
Solve the allocation and report the four amounts.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Set the floor by a three-way balance, not by output alone.
A phased inflow beats one wave because jobs scale with last year's output.

unresolved_questions.question: What allocation does the penalized program actually return?
Does degree really track wealth in this population?
Are the bracket transition rates estimated or assumed?
